rationale: IntMM is a tiny (7 functions, ~1.3 KB text) loop-kernel benchmark whose runtime is dominated by the hot matrix-multiply nest in Intmm/Innerproduct, so the table leans on low-overhead transforms and heavily penalizes cost in hot code: SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain because arithmetic obfuscation directly obscures the multiply-add core at near-zero risk, and IGV is favored because the matrices are globals whose addressing/layout can be disguised cheaply. FLA and BCF carry the highest RuntimeCost weights (0.9) so the selector suppresses them in the hot loops — flattening destroys the tight loop structure and bogus control flow inflates per-iteration branch work — while their security weights keep them viable for cold functions like Initmatrix, main, and _start. IBR and ICALL get moderate-to-high RuntimeCost (0.7-0.8) since indirect branches/calls tax the inner-product call path, and SPLIT stays enabled with low cost weights as a cheap diversifier. CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low across the board (0.1-0.4) because this is small, well-defined integer code where all passes are safe, and SizeCost is moderate only for the control-flow-heavy passes since the tiny binary means relative bloat is the main size concern.
